app_info.subtitle: Access your computer remotely
app_info.description: Remote Arc securely connects ChatGPT and Codex to Windows, macOS, Linux, and explicitly shared Chrome tabs. It can inspect directories and files, read process information, read shared browser tabs, and—only when the user separately enables the required permission—run terminal commands, modify files, or click/fill non-sensitive controls in a specific shared tab. Browser interaction is per-tab, stale snapshot refs are rejected, and recognized password, one-time-code, payment-card, and file-picker fields remain blocked. Each device has an independent revocable credential and policy. Remote Arc uses an OAuth-protected Universal Remote MCP endpoint and an outbound-only device connection. Use it only with computers, files, accounts, and services you own or are authorized to administer.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads account-scoped paired-device metadata and online state without changing any device or account state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Only reads Remote Arc control-plane metadata for devices owned by the authenticated user; it does not access public internet services.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not modify, delete, overwrite, stop, execute, or otherwise change user or external state.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads the enabled and currently available Remote Arc tool list for one device owned by the authenticated user.
justifications.open_world_justification: The result is derived from Remote Arc device policy and capability metadata rather than external public services.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not change the device policy or invoke any device capability.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists metadata for browser tabs the user explicitly shared with Remote Arc without navigating, clicking, or changing page state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads the set of tabs already shared from the user's private browser session and does not itself contact or modify an external service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only returns shared-tab metadata and does not navigate, submit forms, close tabs, or alter browser state.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads metadata for an explicitly shared browser tab without changing the tab or page.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads existing state from the user's shared browser context and performs no external action itself.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not navigate, click, submit, close, or otherwise modify the browser tab.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads a simplified snapshot of the explicitly shared page, including visible text and labels, without modifying the page.
justifications.open_world_justification: Observes content already loaded in the user's shared tab and does not navigate to or modify an external service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not click, type, submit forms, navigate, or change page state.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns text currently selected by the user in an explicitly shared tab without changing the selection or page.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's existing shared browser state and performs no external action.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not navigate, click, type, submit, or mutate the page.

justifications.read_only_justification: Extracts visible links from an explicitly shared page without opening or modifying them.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads link data already present in the user's shared tab and does not follow links or contact their destinations.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not navigate, click links, submit forms, or alter browser state.

justifications.read_only_justification: Extracts rows from a visible table in an explicitly shared page without changing the table or page.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads table data already loaded in the user's shared tab and performs no external action.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not edit page content, navigate, click, or submit anything.

justifications.read_only_justification: Retrieves a directory listing from a paired computer without changing filesystem contents.
justifications.open_world_justification: Operates on the user's private paired computer and does not itself contact or alter public internet services.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only enumerates files and directories and does not write, move, or delete them.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads file contents from a paired computer without modifying the file.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads data from the user's private paired computer rather than from a public or third-party internet service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not write, overwrite, delete, or otherwise mutate the requested file.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads metadata for a file or directory without altering the filesystem.
justifications.open_world_justification: The metadata comes from the user's private paired computer and no public internet side effect is performed.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only inspects metadata and does not modify file or directory state.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads the running-process list from a paired computer without starting, stopping, or modifying processes.
justifications.open_world_justification: Process information is obtained from the user's private device and the tool does not access external services.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not terminate, signal, start, or otherwise change a process.

justifications.read_only_justification: Runs an arbitrary terminal command, so it can change local system state and is not read-only.
justifications.open_world_justification: A terminal command may access or modify public internet services, for example by calling APIs, pushing code, deploying software, or publishing packages.
justifications.destructive_justification: Commands can overwrite or delete local data, change repositories or environments, stop services, or cause irreversible external side effects; Remote Arc therefore treats this tool as consequential.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads status metadata for a Remote Arc-managed background process without changing that process.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads process state from the user's paired computer and does not itself contact external services.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not start, stop, signal, or mutate the managed process.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads captured stdout and stderr from a Remote Arc-managed background process without changing the process.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads output already available on the paired computer and performs no public internet action itself.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not start, stop, signal, or modify the process or its output.

justifications.read_only_justification: Stops a running Remote Arc-managed process and its child process tree, so it changes local system state.
justifications.open_world_justification: The tool acts on a process running on the user's paired computer; it does not directly target a public internet service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Stopping a process can interrupt work, terminate builds or servers, lose in-memory state, or leave operations incomplete.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes or appends file contents on the user's paired computer, so it changes local state.
justifications.open_world_justification: The tool writes to the local filesystem on a paired private computer and does not directly act on an external internet service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Rewrite mode can overwrite existing user data and append mode changes persistent file contents; supported clients may create a local undo snapshot, but mutation remains consequential.

justifications.read_only_justification: Performs targeted search-and-replace in a file on the paired computer, so it changes persistent local data.
justifications.open_world_justification: The operation targets the private local filesystem and does not directly access or mutate a public internet service.
justifications.destructive_justification: A text replacement can alter source code, configuration, or other persistent user data and may overwrite the prior contents.

justifications.read_only_justification: Restores the previous local file state from a Remote Arc undo snapshot, so it mutates the filesystem and is not read-only.
justifications.open_world_justification: Restoration is performed only on the user's paired computer using a local snapshot and does not target external internet services.
justifications.destructive_justification: The operation is specifically a recovery action that restores a prior Remote Arc-created file state and refuses unsafe restoration when the file has changed again, so it is not classified as destructive.

justifications.read_only_justification: Clicks an element in an explicitly shared browser tab and can change page or external state, so it is not read-only.
justifications.open_world_justification: A click may navigate, submit a form, activate a third-party control, or otherwise interact with an external website.
justifications.destructive_justification: A clicked control can trigger consequential or irreversible website actions; Remote Arc therefore requires an explicit per-tab interaction grant and treats the tool as destructive.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes a field in the explicitly shared page, so it is not read-only, even though it does not submit the form by itself.
justifications.open_world_justification: It types into a control on an external website and may influence subsequent actions on that service.
justifications.destructive_justification: The tool only fills an allowed non-sensitive control and does not itself submit or click; recognized password, OTP, payment-card, and file fields are blocked.

test_cases.description: List the authenticated review account's paired devices and identify which are online.
test_cases.user_prompt: Show me my connected computers and tell me which ones are online.
test_cases.expected_output: The response should include the deterministic reviewer device named Review Desktop, identify it as Windows, and report it as online.

test_cases.description: Inspect the deterministic review project and identify its test script.
test_cases.user_prompt: On Review Desktop, list /review-demo, then read /review-demo/package.json and tell me what npm test runs.
test_cases.expected_output: The listing should include package.json, src, and README.md, and the model should identify the test script as vitest run.

test_cases.description: Run the safe deterministic review test command.
test_cases.user_prompt: Run npm test on Review Desktop and summarize the result.
test_cases.expected_output: The deterministic fixture should report 2 passing test suites and 8 passing tests, and the model should summarize that the tests passed.

test_cases.description: Write a file in the isolated review workspace, verify it, and restore the previous state.
test_cases.user_prompt: On Review Desktop, write "review fixture write works" to /review-demo/reviewer-note.txt, read it back to verify the contents, then undo that Remote Arc file change.
test_cases.expected_output: The write should succeed only inside /review-demo, the read should return exactly review fixture write works, and undo_last_change should report that /review-demo/reviewer-note.txt was restored to its previous state.

test_cases.description: Apply a targeted edit in the isolated review workspace, verify it, and undo the change.
test_cases.user_prompt: On Review Desktop, update /review-demo/README.md by replacing "deterministic fixture data" with "isolated deterministic fixture data", read the file to verify the edit, then undo the change.
test_cases.expected_output: edit_block should make exactly one replacement, the verification read should include isolated deterministic fixture data, and undo_last_change should report that /review-demo/README.md was restored.

negative_test_cases.description: Answer a general knowledge question without accessing a paired computer.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Explain the difference between TCP and UDP.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Answer directly without invoking Remote Arc because the request does not require access to a paired computer.

negative_test_cases.description: Summarize content already present in the conversation without accessing a paired computer.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Summarize this sentence: Remote work can reduce commuting time and give people more flexibility.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Summarize the supplied sentence directly. Remote Arc should not be invoked because all required content is already in the conversation.

negative_test_cases.description: Answer a standalone programming question that does not require a local project or terminal.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Write a Python function that removes duplicate values from a list while preserving order.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Provide the Python solution directly without invoking Remote Arc because no local file, project, process, or computer access was requested.
